findings.criterion: Pre-deletion backup of the full comment payload for each affected issue exists before any DELETE, gated on `len(fetched) == total`.
findings.detail: The execution comment (timestamp 1787286317899959001) confirms pre-deletion backups were taken before any delete (3.2/6.9/9.5 MB files). However, the honesty note comment (timestamp 1787286351334756001) explicitly acknowledges: "AC2 specifies the backup be 'gated on `len(fetched) == total`'. I took complete paginated backups but did NOT implement that explicit assertion." The criterion as written requires the gate as a precondition; the operator substituted outcome-based verification (final counts matching the plan) as an equivalent. While the operator's reasoning is sound, the specific precondition gate required by the AC was not implemented.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment confirming that the explicit `len(fetched) == total` assertion was verified by another means (e.g., the paginated fetch log showing total pages fetched matched the Jira-reported total count), or acknowledge this as a known deviation with a future-run note already recorded.
findings.title: AC2 `len(fetched) == total` gate not implemented as specified

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
